findings.reason: the corrected href is a one-line edit that restores §5's evidence pointer, which now 404s.
findings.text: §5's landed-summary links `full record`, a bare extensionless href; the surface fetches `/${project}/${href}.html` (`docs/ui/plan.jsx:669`), resolving this to `/reckon/s5-fenced-claude-carries-its-login.html`, and no such file exists anywhere under `docs/` (searched `find docs -name '*s5-fenced-claude*'`, no result). The evidence actually lives at `docs/evidence/archive/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home-landed.html#s5-fenced-claude-carries-its-login`, the form every other landed section in the repo uses (`/reckon/evidence/archive/-landed.html#`), so a reader following §5's "full record" reaches a missing page.

findings.reason: an implementable section that cannot be shown to fail is exactly the gap the done-when rubric exists to catch, and §6 is the next section a node will build.
findings.text: §6's done-when ("the harness-home carry merges, imas-ambix qualifies fenced clive and one fenced codex launch, and the codex pause is lifted") declares no negative control, so a node dispatched at §6 has no falsifier showing its guard fires; §8 by contrast names one ("restore the appended PYTHONPATH; the test must then fail with the import error"), and the sections already done (§1–§4, §7) each state a control.

findings.reason: splitting §6 by deliverable is what makes each half reviewable, since the cross-repo qualification carries a different done-when and evidence regime than the reckon merge.
findings.text: §6 carries at least four deliverables in one node: merge the declared harness-home carry in reckon, run the clive D4 qualification in imas-ambix, run a controlled codex launch, and lift the codex pause in host config; two of these live outside the reckon repository entirely, so the section cannot be reviewed or closed on one verdict (its gate proves neither the reckon change nor the imas-ambix qualification).

response_events.reason: section 6 is outside this review's wave, which added section 8 only; its missing negative control is left for the section's builder to add before dispatch, not judged wrong

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the §5 landed-summary's "full record" link is a bare extensionless href that does not resolve once `.html` is appended.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6's done-when states only outcomes ("the harness-home carry merges, imas-ambix qualifies fenced clive and one fenced codex launch, and the codex pause is lifted") and names no declared negative control, unlike §8, which names one explicitly.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the landed archive `docs/evidence/archive/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home-landed.html`, the logs and figures under `docs/figures/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home/`, and the per-run gate logs under `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>/` all sit on the operator home or in-repo, not on a node-local temporary path.

rubric_items.wiring: pass — the declared `plan-informs` targets (`new-work-gets-a-new-worker`, `worker-death-is-recorded`) both exist, and the gating edge the fence section owns is carried on the counterpart plan (`the-boundary-check-reads-two-trees` declares `plan-informs: a-worker-cannot-write-your-home`), so no dependency is missing and none points at a nonexistent node.
